title: Marketplace partner sprint kickoff + certification cheat sheet
body:
Purpose:
Quick, practical kickoff doc we hand to a partner integration sprint squad. Combines required gates for marketplace certification + short copy variants + a tight go-live runbook. Not exhaustive — this is a pragmatic checklist for a 2–4 week sprint.

Context / scope:
- Target partner type: ISV connectors and SaaS publishers that want a Redwood tile (hosted listing) in public cloud marketplaces and Redwood Channel (co-sell).
- Goal: MVT listing + certified billing integration + security self-attestation ready within sprint.
- Constraints: partner provides legal/compliance answers and logo assets within week 1.

Sprint roles and channels:
- PM (Redwood): Sasha Patel (owner)
- Partner success lead: Aisha Wang
- Integration engineer: Tom Reynolds
- Security reviewer: Priya Nair
- Slack: #marketplace-partner-onboard
- Jira epic: JIRA-PLAT-312 (linked)

Sprint timeline (example 3-week cadence):
- Week 0 (prep): legal & billing kickoff, tile copy draft, partner asset request sent
- Week 1: dev integration (billing hooks, OAuth / SSO if needed), telemetry contract, tile creative draft
- Week 2: security review, QA acceptance, marketplace pre-submit checklist, initial publisher sandbox test
- Week 3: finalize docs, submit to marketplace, Redwood internal verification, light-weight smoke test, go / rollback decision

MVT acceptance checklist (must pass before submission):
- Copy + creative
  - Final hero (<= 120 chars) and 30/90 char variants prepared
  - One 16:9 hero graphic (1920x1080) and one 1:1 logo (500x500 PNG, transparent) provided
  - Short feature bullets (3) and 3–4 customer benefit lines
- Technical
  - Billing SKU mapping documented (list SKUs and entitlements)
  - OAuth / API keys working in publisher sandbox; test tokens and sample request/response cURL provided
  - Health endpoint and basic readiness + liveness probes (if private deployment) or status page link for hosted API
  - Minimum performance statement (typical p95 latency under expected load)
- Security & compliance
  - Completed partner security QnA form (link to Confluence)
  - KMS/HSM requirements declared (if region-specific) and data residency notes present
  - SLAs/response windows for escalations documented
- QA & telemetry
  - Telemetry events list (tile_click, purchase_initiated, provision_complete, usage_reported) with event schema
  - End-to-end smoke test scenarios (install tile, complete trial purchase, validate API key provisioning)
  - Error modes documented and expected remediation steps
- Legal / commercial
  - Billing contract template signed or sign-off from finance for marketplace pricing
  - Logo / trademark use approved by partner

Copy snippets (examples to iterate quickly)
- Hero (short, 10–20 words): "Run high-performance LLM inference with predictable pricing and enterprise controls."
- 30-char variant: "Low-latency LLM inference, enterprise-ready."
- 90-char variant: "Redwood Inference: predictable, cost-effective LLM serving across hosted, dedicated and private deployments."
- 3 feature bullets (concise):
  - "Predictable throughput and reserved GPU capacity"
  - "Unified API across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments"
  - "Built-in telemetry and rollback for safe rollouts"
- Value prop one-liner for publisher page: "Plug into a production-first inference platform designed for SLOs, cost control, and easy rollouts."

Marketplace tile copy guidance (do's and don'ts):
- Do: use active verbs, call out outcomes (e.g., reduce inference cost, improve p95 latency).
- Do: include compatibility (e.g., "Supports common open models + customer model pinning").
- Don’t: include pricing numbers that conflict with marketplace SKU mapping—leave price fields as the SKU responsibility.
- Don’t: claim certifications you have not validated in partner region (e.g., GDPR vs local law nuance).

Telemetry & logging contract (minimum):
- Required events: tile_view, tile_click, license_provisioned, usage_batch_sent, error_reported
- Each event must include: timestamp, actor_id (anonymized ID allowed), platform_sku, region, status_code, duration_ms (if relevant)
- Error reporting: partner must surface 5xx incidents to #marketplace-partner-onboard and open a Jira ticket within 1 business hour for P1s

Technical gating matrix (quick):
- Billing hooks: must implement POST /billing/ack with idempotency key -> acceptance response 200
- Provisioning: API returns provision_id and provisioning_state within 10s for typical flows
- Secrets: support rotating API keys and publish revocation endpoint or instructions

QA acceptance scenarios (compact list):
- S1: Install tile -> complete trial purchase -> validate license_provisioned event -> ensure 200 OK responses for first 100 requests
- S2: Simulate failure (downstream model OOM) -> tile shows graceful degradation and returns structured error with retry-info
- S3: Billing webhook duplicate delivery -> idempotency ensures single invoice item

Pre-submit checklist (one pager for partner portal):
- [ ] Finalized copy variants (hero + 30 + 90)
- [ ] Creative assets uploaded (logo + hero)
- [ ] Billing SKU list & price tiers mapped and validated with finance
- [ ] Security QnA complete and signed off
- [ ] Telemetry contract accepted by platform team
- [ ] At least 3 successful smoke-run tests in sandbox
- [ ] Jira tickets for any known minor defects with clear owners and ETA

Go / rollback plan (decision criteria):
- Go if: all MVT acceptance items pass, no P1 defects, marketplace validation returns green, partner legal sign-off obtained
- Rollback triggers: unexpected billing failures impacting customers, repeated 5xx on provisioning > 1% for 30m, security red flags from audit
- Rollback steps: disable tile in marketplace dashboard -> revert billing hooks -> post-mortem within 48 hrs -> customer outreach plan drafted

Post-launch 30-day quick metrics to track:
- Tile installs and trial-to-paid conversion rate
- Avg and p95 inference latency reported via telemetry
- Billing events success rate and revenue by SKU
- Support tickets opened vs closed by SLA window

Notes / gotchas from past launches (ops memory):
- Partners often deliver logos late; start creative review in week 0
- SKU granularity mismatch: insist on 1–2 trial SKUs + 1 baseline paid SKU for MVT to simplify finance mapping
- Telemetry payload size: ask partners to batch events; large per-request telemetry killed initial sandbox runs

Quick links and artifacts to attach before submit:
- Partner security QnA template: CONFLUENCE-4567
- Billing mapping spreadsheet: github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-billing/blob/main/mapping.xlsx
- Marketplace tile spec template (internal): github.com/redwood-inference/marketplace-specs/blob/main/tile-spec.md

Immediate next steps for this partner sprint (action items):
1) Sasha: send creative asset request + copy template by EOD (owner: Sasha)
2) Partner: confirm billing SKU list and provide sandbox account credentials by day 3
3) Tom: stub billing webhook locally and validate idempotency by day 5
4) Priya: run security self-attestation and flag any infra KMS needs by day 7

Open questions / items to resolve in sprint:
- Does partner require private deployment options ahead of listing, or is hosted enough for MVT?
- What marketplace-specific legal clauses (reseller vs direct) need finance sign-off?

This doc is a short-running playbook. Use it as the sprint checklist, paste final copy into publisher portal, and attach the linked artifacts. If we need to expand into a full runbook, we’ll spin a companion doc with detailed API sample payloads and webhook replay scripts.
